title: Alvarez: assisting grace prior in the order of causality
source_text: LXII. Contra vero pertendunt alii gratiam adjuvantem atque cooperantem, secundum causalitatis ordinem, praevenire liberum arbitrium, & prius quam illud agere: Ac quanquam simul tempore tam gratia, quam liberum arbitrium influant in piam operationem, natura tamen quodammodo priorem esse gratiae influxum, nec ordine causalitatis cum influxu liberi arbitrii simultaneum. Haec est sententia Didaci Alvares in Epitome de Auxiliis divinae gratiae, libro tertio, capite decimo nono, cujus hoc lemma est, Quod Gratia cooperans, in quantum cooperans, sit praeveniens, seu praemovens liberum arbitrium ad consensum, & non solum pariter, & simultanee cum illo in piam operationem influens. Idem vero caput his verbis incipit, Ex praemissis constat, quod gratia cooperans, quatenus ab excitante distinguitur, sit praeveniens liberam cooperationem arbitrii creati, non quidem prioritate temporis, sed rationis duntaxat & causalitatis.
pass_a_gloss: LXII. But on the contrary others maintain that helping and cooperating grace, according to the order of causality, goes before free choice, and acts before it: And although at the same time in time both grace, and free choice flow into the pious operation, yet the influx of grace is in a certain way prior in nature, and not simultaneous in order of causality with the influx of free choice. This is the opinion of Diego Alvarez in the Epitome on the Helps of divine grace, book three, chapter nineteen, whose heading is this, That cooperating Grace, insofar as cooperating, is prevenient, or premoving free choice to consent, and not only equally, and simultaneously with it flowing into the pious operation. But the same chapter begins with these words, From the premises it is established, that cooperating grace, insofar as it is distinguished from rousing, is prevenient to the free cooperation of created choice, not indeed by priority of time, but of reason only and of causality.
pass_b_english: Thesis LXII. Others, on the contrary, maintain that assisting and cooperating grace comes before free choice in the order of causality and acts before it does. Although grace and free choice act on the devout work at the same time, the influence of grace is in some way prior in nature, and is not simultaneous with the influence of free choice in the order of causality.

This is the view of Diego Alvarez in the Epitome of his work on the helps of divine grace, book 3, chapter 19, whose heading is: 'That cooperating grace, as cooperating, is prevenient, or premoves free choice to consent, and does not merely act on the devout work equally and simultaneously with it.'

The chapter itself begins: 'From what has been laid down it is clear that cooperating grace, insofar as it is distinguished from rousing grace, goes before the free cooperation of created choice, not by priority in time but only in reason and causality.'
